newsitem.title: USA: Mass. House passes convention center bill.
newsitem.headline: Mass. House passes convention center bill.

text.p: The Massachusetts House of Representatives overwhelmingly passed a bill on Tuesday approving $700 million funding for a convention center in Boston by a vote of 134 to 20.
Massachusetts Governor William Weld had threatened to veto the bill if it fails to give voters a chance to approve the necessary tax hikes, but the legislation passed by a comfortable majority.

A Republican amendment to put before the voters the hotel/motel tax in Boston, Cambridge, Worcester and Springfield that would help fund the state's share of the convention center went down to defeat on Monday 120 to 30.

"The increase in this bill, in our hotel/motel tax, is borne principally if not exclusively by people from Kansas and Texas and Florida and other states who will come here for a few days if not several days," House Speaker Thomas Finneran said on Tuesday.
Finneran said a new convention center, coupled with Boston's historical, cultural and educational sites, make the city an attractive destination for conventions.
"Purely on the economics and the job creation, i think we would be remiss if we missed this opportunity," he said.
Under the accord's terms, Boston's share of the project to be financed by bonds will come to $157 million, some $27 million more than Mayor Thomas Menino said the city could afford.
The bill will now go before the Senate Ways and Means Committee.
